{{Short description|Sporadic simple group}}
{{for|general background and history of the Conway sporadic groups|Conway group}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Conway group Co<sub>3</sub>}}
{{Group theory sidebar |Finite}}

In the area of modern algebra known as [[group theory]], the '''Conway group''' ''<math>\mathrm{Co}_3</math>'' is a [[sporadic simple group]] of [[Order (group theory)|order]]
:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;495,766,656,000
: = 2<sup>10</sup>{{·}}3<sup>7</sup>{{·}}5<sup>3</sup>{{·}}7{{·}}11{{·}}23
: ≈ 5{{e|11}}.

==History and properties==
''<math>\mathrm{Co}_3</math>'' is one of the 26 sporadic groups and was discovered by {{harvs|txt |authorlink=John Horton Conway |last=Conway |first=John Horton| year1=1968 |year2=1969}} as the [[Automorphism group|group of automorphisms]] of the [[Leech lattice]] <math>\Lambda</math> fixing a lattice vector of type 3, thus length {{radic|6}}. It is thus a subgroup of [[Conway group|<math>\mathrm{Co}_0</math>]]. It is isomorphic to a subgroup of <math>\mathrm{Co}_1</math>. The direct product <math>2\times \mathrm{Co}_3</math> is maximal in <math>\mathrm{Co}_0</math>.

The [[Schur multiplier]] and the [[outer automorphism group]] are both [[Trivial group|trivial]].

== Representations ==

Co<sub>3</sub> acts on a 23-dimensional even lattice with no roots, given by the [[orthogonal complement]] of a norm 6 vector of the Leech lattice. This gives 23-dimensional representations over any field; over fields of characteristic 2 or 3 this can be reduced to a 22-dimensional faithful representation.

Co<sub>3</sub> has a doubly transitive [[permutation representation]] on 276 points.

{{harvs|txt|last=Feit|first=Walter|authorlink=Walter Feit|year=1974}} showed that if a finite group has an absolutely irreducible faithful rational representation of dimension 23 and has no subgroups of index 23 or 24 then it is contained in either <math>\Z/2\Z \times \mathrm{Co}_2</math> or <math>\Z/2\Z \times \mathrm{Co}_3</math>.

== Maximal subgroups ==
Some maximal subgroups fix or reflect 2-dimensional sublattices of the Leech lattice. It is usual to define these planes by [[Conway group#Sublattice groups|'''h-k-l triangles''']]: triangles including the origin as a vertex, with edges (differences of vertices) being vectors of types ''h'', ''k'', and ''l''.

{{harvs|txt|last=Finkelstein|first=Larry|year=1973}} found the 14 conjugacy classes of maximal subgroups of <math>\mathrm{Co}_3</math> as follows:

==Generalized Monstrous Moonshine==

In analogy to [[monstrous moonshine]] for the monster ''M'', for ''Co''<sub>3</sub>, the relevant McKay-Thompson series is <math>T_{4A}(\tau)</math> where one can set the constant term a(0) = 24 ({{OEIS2C|id=A097340}}),

:<math>\begin{align}j_{4A}(\tau)
&=T_{4A}(\tau)+24\\
&=\Big(\tfrac{\eta^2(2\tau)}{\eta(\tau)\,\eta(4\tau)} \Big)^{24} \\
&=\Big(\big(\tfrac{\eta(\tau)}{\eta(4\tau)}\big)^{4}+4^2 \big(\tfrac{\eta(4\tau)}{\eta(\tau)}\big)^{4}\Big)^2\\
&=\frac{1}{q} + 24+ 276q + 2048q^2 +11202q^3+49152q^4+\dots
\end{align}</math>

and ''η''(''τ'') is the [[Dedekind eta function]].
